attempts.label: DANDI:001750
attempts.paper_title: Cell Atlas and Novel Signal Processing Strategy in Primate Insular Cortex
attempts.entry_title: Somatic Na+ currents of VENs and PCs in macaque insular cortex (Liu et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Here is the paragraph, ready to save to that file: The paper's main findings mostly could not be tested here, and those that held rest on the authors' own tables. The lower Na+ current in von Economo neurons was not confirmed, since it was significant under only 2 of 8 readings and the paper does not say how the maximal current was measured. Larger eEPSPs, the lowest phase peak index and similar VEN subtypes held, checking statistics but not measurements. The metabolite gradient did not reproduce (175 differences against 228), and the glycolytic bias held for citrate and glutamate only. Model, sequencing, connectivity and morphology findings went untested for lack of runnable code or time.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Liu, Huang, Shen, Shao, Jing et al. (2026) that rest on dandiset 001750, which holds 35 outside-out patch recordings of somatic Na+ currents from one macaque. It links the files to the paper's per-cell table, compares the maximal Na+ current of VENs and L5 PCs under each reading of the method, and checks the VEN to PC ratio and the patch size. It also tests the metabolomics findings on MetaboLights MTBLS13927, and the eEPSP amplitude ANOVA, the VEN subtype comparisons and the phase peak index comparison on the paper's own tables.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Liu et al. (2026) from dandiset 001750

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's recordings are the 35 outside-out patches of the paper's code table (14 VEN and 21 PC), and the maximal Na+ current computed from each recording agrees with the value the table gives for it.
outcomes.source: Data availability; github.com/RFLiu2021/AIC_proj at commit 44cd8a6, ephysio/data_ephy/rawdata_ephysio/metadata_outSideOutSodiumCurrentRec.csv
outcomes.quote: https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/001750 (sodium channel currents)
outcomes.notes: All 35 files match the 35 rows of the code table by file name, and every table cell ID agrees with the file's electrode cell_id in session and cell number (35 of 35). The dataset carries no cell type, so none can disagree with the table (14 VEN, 21 PC). Under the criterion's eight readings at most 2 of 35 computed maxima are within 10% of the table, short of the 28 required. The as-recorded readings (a1) are a median 4.15 to 4.61 times the table, because the traces keep holding currents of tens of pA. The baseline-subtracted readings (a2) are a median 1.32 to 1.40 times the table, Spearman 0.47 to 0.68, and a2b1c1 agrees best. Under a2b1c1, 11 maxima (6 VEN, 5 PC) lie later than 3 ms after the onset or at steps below -55 mV, and in 10 cells (6 VEN, 4 PC) the maximum is a brief biphasic transient 0.07 to 0.16 ms wide (every other maximum is 0.33 ms or wider), an artefact; their ratio to the table is a median 1.94 against 1.28 for the other cells. Noise SD (median 6.9 pA in VENs, 9.6 pA in PCs, p = 0.34) and repetition count (2.5 against 3, p = 0.89) do not differ by type. Bessel filters at 2.9, 5 and 10 kHz (4-pole, run once forward) and a 0 to 3 ms window bring at most 3 of 35 within 10%. A moving average before the peak gives 19 of 35 at 0.5 ms and at most 26 of 35 at 0.75 ms (median ratio 1.006, Spearman 0.982), below the criterion's 28, and that width was chosen as the best fit to the table. No measure tried matches the table to the criterion's tolerance; the smoothed peak comes closest. None of these variants is a reading of the paper, and none decides.
deviations: The link's value comparison used the eight readings of fig4d-sodium-current-lower, as the criterion says. The smoothing variant is the attempt's own and decides nothing.

outcomes.statement: Somatic Na+ currents recorded in outside-out patches are significantly lower in VENs (n = 14) than in L5 PCs (n = 21).
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 4d
outcomes.quote: outside-out patch-clamp recording showed that the somatic Na + currents evoked in VENs ( n = 14) were significantly lower than those of L5 PCs ( n = 21) (Fig. 4d )
outcomes.notes: The counts are 14 VEN and 21 PC, as stated. The VEN median is lower under all eight readings, but significance differs between them. Rank-sum p is 0.045 (a1b1c1) and 0.025 (a1b1c2), and 0.077 to 0.29 under the six others, so by the criterion the claim is blocked. Both significant readings keep each patch's holding current in the measure, but the other two a1 readings, over all steps, do not find the effect (a1b2c1 p = 0.27, a1b2c2 p = 0.18). Under the code's example reading (a2 b1 c1), VEN 30.4 against PC 38.1 pA, p = 0.10. By session under that reading, VEN is lower in HS (15.9 against 40.3 pA, 7 and 11 cells, p = 0.0028) and not in AS (40.7 against 36.2 pA, 7 and 10 cells, p = 0.60). In the code table's values VENs are lower in both sessions (HS 12.4 against 31.5 pA, p = 0.0028; AS 17.5 against 29.1 pA, ratio 0.60, p = 0.11), so only the significance rests on HS. The AS reversal under a2 b1 c1 is mostly the artefact, not a session effect. Under that reading, the only one for which widths were computed, the maximum is a brief transient in 10 cells (6 of 14 VENs, 4 of 21 PCs), and 9 of them are in AS (5 of its 7 VENs, 4 of its 10 PCs; the one in HS is HS1c18). Three AS VEN transients are 3 to 5 times the table's value (AS4c14 70.7 against 15.5 pA, AS3c11 87.7 against 17.5, AS1c1 42.1 against 13.8). Without the transient cells AS keeps 2 VENs and 6 PCs (37.2 against 34.3 pA, p = 0.86), too few to tell, and HS keeps its difference (15.6 against 40.3 pA, p = 0.0019). In variants that are not readings of the paper and decide nothing, a 4-pole Bessel low-pass run once forward as an amplifier's filter acts (2.9, 5 or 10 kHz, cut-offs fixed in advance) and a 0 to 3 ms window, 13 of the 24 baseline-subtracted variants give p < 0.05, every a2 reading at 2.9 kHz, every one with the short window, and a2b1c2 at 5 kHz. The paper's code table gives 14.9 against 29.3 pA, p = 0.001, and the smoothed variant 16.0 against 29.9 pA, p = 0.0008, but that variant was fitted to the table. The t-test variant gives p = 0.013 to 0.96 over the readings. Whether the criterion should include a filtered reading is asked of a reader (questions/001750.yaml). Current density cannot be computed, as no capacitance is stored. Question for the paper's authors (finding methods_unavailable) is how the maximal current was measured from the traces. It asks which baseline was used, whether the traces were filtered or the peak fitted, and over which steps and window. Two of the four readings that subtract no baseline find the effect (a1b1c1, a1b1c2), and none with the code's own baseline subtraction does, unless the trace is filtered, smoothed or the window cut short.
deviations: Cell types come from the paper's code table through na-cell-table-link, as the files carry none.

Repetitions were averaged before the peak was taken (criterion). The baseline window of reading a2 is 18.0 to 19.0 ms, the first 100 samples of a cut starting 2 ms before the onset at 100 kHz, as in Fig4d_plotNaCurrent.m.

outcomes.statement: The VEN model's somatodendritic Na+ conductance (55 pS/um2, against 80 pS/um2 in the PC model) was set from the recorded ratio of peak Na+ current in VENs to PCs, which puts that ratio near 55/80, about 0.69.
outcomes.source: Methods, Computational model, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The VEN model's somatodendritic conductance (55 pS µm −2 ) was set based on the experimentally recorded ratio of peak sodium current in VENs relative to PCs. (Fig. 4d )
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig4d-sodium-current-lower, which is blocked. The ratios were computed for every reading of the measure. They are 0.68 to 0.99, and in tolerance (0.619 to 0.756) under some summary only for the four as-recorded readings (a1), whose values include each patch's holding current. The baseline-subtracted readings give 0.79 to 0.99. The code table's values give 0.58 (mean) and 0.51 (median), and the smoothed variant 0.58 and 0.54, none in tolerance. In the non-deciding filtered and short-window variants, 10 of 24 baseline-subtracted variants give a ratio in tolerance under some summary. The Extended Data Fig. 7c legend says the conductance range was also set from previous publications, so 55 pS/um2 may not be the recorded ratio alone.

outcomes.statement: The outside-out patches have a capacitance of about 50 fF, a membrane area of about 5 um2 at 1 uF/cm2, and similar membrane areas were sampled from both cell types.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiological recording, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: No differences in the degree or time of suction applied to the back of pipettes were required to form high resistance (3–10 GΩ) seals at somatic sites, suggesting that similar membrane areas were sampled ... the membrane surface area (~5 µm 2 ) of outside-out patches was calculated from the capacitance (~50 fF) assuming a specific membrane capacitance of 1 µF cm −2
outcomes.notes: No VoltageClampSeries in any file holds a capacitance, compensation or series resistance value (only data, electrode, gain and starting_time). Every file holds the same 52 values and attributes outside the data series, all printed; the IntracellularElectrode has only cell_id, description and location, there is no lab_meta_data and no notes, and none of them, nor the metadata of any of the 35 assets, names a capacitance, resistance, seal or compensation. The Methods say the traces were leak subtracted online, which would also remove the capacitive transients from which a capacitance might be estimated; this is inferred from the Methods, and no such estimate was tried. The paper's code table holds no capacitance either.

outcomes.statement: Of 581 metabolites, 228 differ between AIC and V1 and only 108 between AIC and parietal cortex.
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical metabolomics reveals a glycolytic bias of the AIC, paragraph 1; Figure 8a
outcomes.quote: we identified 228 differentially abundant metabolites between the AIC and V1 (Welch's ANOVA test followed by Games–Howell test, P < 0.05) compared with only 108 between the AIC and PrC
outcomes.notes: On the deposited values, Welch's ANOVA at P < 0.05 followed by Games-Howell at P < 0.05 gives 175 metabolites for AIC against V1 (expected 205.2 to 250.8) and 84 for AIC against PrC (expected 97.2 to 118.8). Games-Howell alone gives 179 and 85. On log2 values the counts are 190 and 95 (194 and 98 without the ANOVA gate), also outside tolerance; the one zero value (L-Cystine, clipped before log2) does not change them. The direction holds under every variant, with about twice as many differences against V1 as against PrC. The deposited table holds 558 metabolites against the 581 the Results report, which may account for part of the shortfall. The samples are 6 AIC, 6 PrC and 7 V1, as the Fig. 8 legend gives.
deviations: The Methods name no transform of the peak areas. The deposited values are used, and log2 values are a variant; both fall short.

The words "followed by" are read as the pair counted when Welch's ANOVA gives P < 0.05; the pair test alone is shown and also falls short. Games-Howell was computed with the studentized range for three groups and Welch degrees of freedom.

outcomes.statement: Compared with V1, AIC shows elevated citrate, reduced 2-ketobutyrate and increased glutamate, read as a glycolytic bias.
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical metabolomics reveals a glycolytic bias of the AIC, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 8d,e
outcomes.quote: AIC cells displayed elevated citrate and reduced 2-ketobutyrate levels, along with increased glutamate
outcomes.notes: Citric acid is higher in AIC than in V1 (ratio 1.37, Games-Howell p = 0.00046) and L-glutamic acid too (ratio 1.35, p = 0.0001). 2-Ketobutyric acid is lower (ratio 0.37) but not significantly (Games-Howell p = 0.18, Welch's ANOVA p = 0.17; on log2 values p = 0.086). Two of the three parts hold. A second entry named "Glutamic acid glutamate" is higher (1.18) without significance (p = 0.15); had it been taken as glutamate, only citrate would hold. The criterion defines no partial outcome; the outcome follows the protocol's definition, an effect that holds only in part.
deviations: Metabolites were found by name in the deposited table; citrate is "Citric acid", glutamate "L-Glutamic acid", 2-ketobutyrate "2-Ketobutyric acid". The paper does not say which table entries it plotted. Glutamate is taken as "L-Glutamic acid", the entry named as the amino acid itself; the notebook selects it explicitly and shows the other entry as a variant.

outcomes.statement: eEPSP amplitudes are higher in VENs than in adjacent PCs, with effects of cell type and stimulation level in an ANOVA.
outcomes.source: Results, VENs respond robustly to deep-layer synaptic input, paragraph 1; Figure 4j
outcomes.quote: whereas the response amplitudes in VENs were significantly higher than those in adjacent PCs (analysis of variance (ANOVA), P = 0.0034 for cell type and P < 0.001 for stimulation level
outcomes.notes: In the 26 VEN-PC pairs of sumData_StimWM.xlsx the VEN amplitudes are higher at each of the three stimulation levels (means 0.0067, 0.0133 and 0.0193 against 0.0036, 0.0066 and 0.0128, unit not stated) and in 21 of 26 pairs. Cell type effect, ordinary two-way ANOVA F = 7.62, p = 0.0065, and repeated-measures ANOVA with the pair as subject F = 8.72, p = 0.0068 (paper P = 0.0034). Stimulation level, p = 5.3e-05 and 1.6e-08. The table holds amplitudes already measured by the authors, so this checks the statistics, not the selection of monosynaptic eEPSPs. The same sheet's "re-orgnized data" block, with the stimulation value on every row, shares 69 of its 78 rows with the copied block and differs in 9; its two-way ANOVA gives cell type p = 0.0033 (paper 0.0034), VENs higher at every level, so the paper's test was most likely run on that block.
deviations: Tested on the paper's per-pair amplitude table, as the claims file names it, not on raw recordings, whose dandiset the paper does not name. In the copied block levels are taken by their order within each pair, as 9 rows give no stimulation value; the re-organized block, with explicit levels, is the cross-check.

outcomes.statement: In Pan-Nav stained sections the AIS of VENs lies farther from the soma than that of PCs, and VENs have a shorter AIS.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 2; Figure 3c
outcomes.quote: showed that the AIS in VENs was, on average, located significantly farther from the soma than in PCs (Fig. 3c ). Additionally, VENs had a shorter AIS than PCs.
outcomes.notes: AIScmp_PCvsVEN_Fig5c.xlsx holds AIS length and distance per cell by type (500 PC and 120 VEN values) with no slice or animal, so neither reading of the two-way ANOVA can be formed. Its counts differ from the legend's 430 PCs and 108 VENs. As a description that decides nothing, the VEN median distance is 15.85 against 3.95 um for PCs, and length 24.33 against 29.13 um (rank-sum p = 3.1e-42 and 2.3e-16), the directions the claim states.

outcomes.statement: In the PC model, lowering the somatodendritic Na+ conductance over the tested range (80 to 55 pS/um2, defined by experimental data and previous publications) only modestly changes the AP (slightly lower and broader) and does not produce the saddle-like phase-plane shape.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 5; Extended Data Figure 7c
outcomes.quote: A reduction in somatodendritic Na + channel density in the PC model only produced modest changes in AP shape (slightly lower amplitude, broader width) but did not induce the saddle-like phase–plane pattern.

outcomes.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 5d
outcomes.quote: In total, we tested 1,292 potential connections from an additional set of 377 neurons in layer 5b and confirmed 31 monosynaptic connections.
outcomes.notes: The criterion assigns the test to the claims file of DANDI:001751 (multi-patch recordings, 301 files, about 7 GB, version 0.260825.0222). It was not repeated in this attempt, which had five hours for 34 claims; the data are public there.

outcomes.statement: VENs form no connections with VENs (0 of 110), PCs (0 of 200) or interneurons (0 of 55), receive none from interneurons (0 of 55) and one in 200 PC-to-VEN pairs, while PCs connect to PCs in 24 of 503 pairs.
outcomes.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 5i
outcomes.quote: PCs formed monosynaptic connections with other PCs in 24 out of 503 tested pairs ... VENs did not form synaptic connections with adjacent VENs (VEN-to-VEN, 0 of 110, 135.7 ± 60.0 μm) or with PCs (VEN-to-PC, 0 of 200, 119.3 ± 63.1 μm). Likewise, VENs received minimal local excitatory input, suggesting PCs rarely projected to VENs (PC-to-VEN, 1 of 200 ... no synaptic connections were found between VENs and INs (VEN-to-IN, 0 of 55 and IN-to-VEN, 0 of 55

outcomes.source: Results, Transcriptomic landscape of the macaque AIC, paragraph 2; Figure 1b,c
outcomes.quote: we categorized these cells into four main classes: excitatory neurons (21,733 cells, 17.8%), inhibitory neurons (17,007 cells, 13.9%), glial cells (83,283 cells, 67.8%) and vascular cells (640 cells, 0.5%)
outcomes.notes: GEO GSE319557 holds FASTQ reads of 122,663 cells; aligning and clustering them is beyond the runner and the notebook's 60 minutes. The processed data on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.18814764) are a multi-part RAR archive of about 11.8 GB that cannot be streamed.
outcomes.where: GEO GSE319557 (10x scRNA-seq, FASTQ, per the Data availability statement); processed data in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.18814764

outcomes.notes: As scrna-classes; the cluster labels are in the processed data on Zenodo, a multi-part RAR archive of about 11.8 GB.

outcomes.statement: VENs have lower firing rates and greater variability in spike timing than PCs.
outcomes.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Supplementary Tables 1 and 2
outcomes.quote: Notably, VENs exhibit lower firing rate and greater variability in spike timing than PCs
outcomes.notes: The criterion blocks the claim as methods_underspecified unless the paper's values and tests (Supplementary Tables 1 and 2) are supplied, since the text names no measure of spike-timing variability; they were not supplied. The data are also large, DANDI:001746 (462 files, about 14.7 GB, version 0.260825.0222); streaming 001750's 0.33 GB took 150 to 256 s in this attempt's runs, so 001746 would take about 1.9 to 3.2 hours to stream before any analysis, beyond the notebook's 60 minutes.

outcomes.statement: VENs have lower AP phase-plane peak indices than every PC type.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 3e
outcomes.quote: The VENs had lower phase peak indices than any type of PCs (Fig. 3e )
outcomes.notes: The VEN median phase peak index (0.117, 29 cells) is the lowest of the six types (0.223 to 0.338 for the others). Kruskal-Wallis p = 4.9e-08, and Dunn's test separates VENs from every PC type, Bonferroni p = 1.5e-07 to 0.001 (unadjusted 1e-08 to 6.8e-05). The sheet's counts (30 L2/3 IT HPCAL1, 21 IT RORB, 121 L5 IT, 29 VEN, 17 L5 ET, 13 L6 PC) differ in four types from the Fig. 2d-f counts the legend refers to (30, 17, 119, 22, 16, 13), so the selection is not exactly the paper's.
deviations: Tested on the paper's per-cell table in its code repository at 44cd8a6 (ephysio/data_ephy/PeakIdx_Fig5e.xlsx, Sheet1), not on the recordings of DANDI:001746 the claims file points to, which were not streamed (see ven-firing-rate-variability). This checks the statistics on the authors' values and their type labels, not the measure. The mean, std and SE rows under each column are dropped, keeping rows named by a cell ID.

The p adjustment of Dunn's test is not in the legend; the sheet's statistics tab names Bonferroni-corrected p values. Both unadjusted and Bonferroni p are shown, and both are below 0.05 for every PC type.

outcomes.statement: In 281 VENs and 306 L5 PCs, APs of VENs are broader and lower in amplitude.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 4a-c
outcomes.quote: APs in VENs were broader and had a lower amplitude compared with L5 PCs (Fig. 4a-c )
outcomes.notes: The claims file points to DANDI:001746, though the paper does not say which dandiset holds these 587 recordings; streaming it would take about 1.9 to 3.2 hours (see ven-firing-rate-variability). No table in the paper's code repository holds AP width and amplitude for 281 VENs and 306 PCs.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001746 (the paper does not say which dandiset holds these recordings)

outcomes.statement: VEN-L and VEN-S have similar physiological properties.
outcomes.source: Results, Multimodal profiling of two VEN subtypes, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 9c-f; Supplementary Table 8
outcomes.quote: Despite their distinct morphological and transcriptomic profiles, both VEN subtypes exhibited similar physiological properties (Extended Data Fig. 9 and Supplementary Table 8 )

statistics.about: eEPSP amplitude, VEN-L against VEN-S (pairs of Extended Data Fig. 9e,f)

outcomes.notes: None of the three tests is significant. AP half-width is a median 3.28 ms in 85 VEN-L and 3.30 ms in 41 VEN-S (rank-sum p = 0.55), AP amplitude 85.9 and 87.1 mV (p = 0.27), BH q = 0.55 and 0.54 over the two. The two-way ANOVA (subtype and stimulation level) of the eEPSP amplitudes of 12 VEN-L and 12 VEN-S gives p = 0.958 for subtype (paper p = 0.9852). The paired comparisons with PCs come out as the legend gives them (VEN-L p = 0.051 against 0.0500, VEN-S p = 0.037 against 0.0355). The counts (85, 41, 12, 12, and two VENs without a subtype) match the Extended Data Fig. 9 legend. The other features of Supplementary Table 8 were not read, as the criterion says.
deviations: Tested on the paper's per-cell tables in its code repository at 44cd8a6 (VENsubtypeCmp_extFig8ab/VENsubtype_APs.mat, read by extFig9ad_plotVENsubtypeAP_Cmp.m, and column J of sumData_StimWM.xlsx), not on the recordings of DANDI:001746 the claims file points to, which were not streamed (see ven-firing-rate-variability). This checks the statistics on the authors' measurements, not the measurements.

The FDR family is not stated (the code's calFDR_VENsubtype_ephysio.m corrects over every feature of a different, Patch-seq table). Benjamini-Hochberg over the two AP tests is shown; since a BH q is never below its raw p and both raw p exceed 0.05, no family can change the result.

outcomes.statement: Among projection neuron subclasses, L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons stand out with a small membrane time constant and a narrow AP width.
outcomes.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Figure 2d,f
outcomes.quote: L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons stood out with a small membrane time constant (tau) and narrow action potential (AP) width (Fig. 2d–f )
outcomes.notes: DANDI:001746 with the transcriptomic subclasses from GSE319369; see ven-firing-rate-variability and patchseq-mapping. The code repository's Ins_patchseq_ephs.xlsx holds tau and AP half-width per Patch-seq cell, but with cluster numbers, not subclass names; subclass names per cell would have to be taken from the table of another figure (PeakIdx_Fig5e.xlsx), whose counts differ from the Fig. 2 legend, and this was not done.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001746 (Patch-seq electrophysiology), with the transcriptomic subclasses from GEO GSE319369 mapped as in the Methods

outcomes.statement: The axons of VENs emanate from their basal dendrite, while those of PCs originate at the base of the soma.
outcomes.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 1; Figure 3a,b
outcomes.quote: One of the most notable morphological features that distinguish VENs from other PC types is that the axons of the VENs emanate from its basal dendrite (Fig. 3a )
outcomes.notes: The morphologies are public on NeuroMorpho.org (doi:10.13021/y4be-0p18). Reading and tracing the axon origin of each reconstruction was not attempted in this run's time.

outcomes.statement: VEN-L has a larger basal dendritic arborization than L5 PCs, VEN-S an intermediate one similar to PCs; the axon origin lies farther from the soma in both VEN subtypes than in PCs, with no difference between VEN-L and VEN-S.
outcomes.source: Results, Multimodal profiling of two VEN subtypes, paragraph 1; Figure 6c-e
outcomes.quote: VEN-L had larger basal dendritic arborization than L5 PCs, whereas VEN-S had intermediate-sized basal dendrite arborization similar to PCs ... the distance from the axon originating site to the soma was significantly greater in both VEN subtypes compared with PCs (Fig. 6e ), with no significant difference observed between VEN-L and VEN-S
outcomes.notes: NeuroMorpho.org morphologies (doi:10.13021/y4be-0p18), not attempted in this run's time.

findings.statement: The files carry no cell type, so VENs and PCs cannot be told apart from the dandiset. Types come only from the paper's code table metadata_outSideOutSodiumCurrentRec.csv, which names each NWB file; the file names and electrode cell IDs agree with it for all 35 patches.
No file holds the patch capacitance, series resistance or compensation values, so the patch size the Methods report (about 50 fF, 5 um2) and current densities cannot be computed.

How the maximal Na+ current was measured from the traces is not stated in the paper or its code. Plain peaks of the repetition-averaged traces, with or without a pre-step baseline, do not match the code table (at most 2 of 35 within 10%), and the VEN against PC difference is significant only under two readings without baseline subtraction. With a 2.9 kHz Bessel low-pass, or a 0 to 3 ms window, it is significant under every baseline-subtracted reading. A peak after 0.75 ms smoothing comes closest to the table (26 of 35 within 10%, 19 of 35 at 0.5 ms), at a width fitted to it. Question for the authors, which baseline, filter or fit, steps and window gave the maximal currents of Fig. 4d?

Every file gives the session start time 2018-01-01 01:00, while the session ids and the code table's cell IDs date the recordings to 6 December 2022. The series starting_time values (0 to 3 s) carry no order.

The traces keep holding currents of -131 to +92 pA before the step although the Methods say they were leak subtracted online, so a baseline must be removed before a peak is taken. One file (cell HS018, a VEN) has a positive holding current and noise near 57 pA SD. Files hold 28 or 34 steps (to +55 or +85 mV) and 1 to 10 repetitions, where the Methods describe steps to 0 mV.

The MetaboLights metabolite table of MTBLS13927 holds 558 identified metabolites, where the Results report 581, and one AIC sample is named A1C-1-Q. The Welch and Games-Howell counts on it fall short of the reported 228 and 108.

In the paper's code repository, AIScmp_PCvsVEN_Fig5c.xlsx has 500 PC and 120 VEN values where the Fig. 3c legend gives 430 and 108, and no slice or animal column for its two-way ANOVA. sumData_StimWM.xlsx gives stimulation values 0.5, 1 and 2 labelled mA where the Methods give 0.05 to 0.2 mA, and no unit for the amplitudes.

In at least 10 of the 35 files the repetition-averaged trace holds brief biphasic transients about 0.1 ms wide (0.07 to 0.16 ms at half height), larger than the Na+ current in some patches (for example AS3c11, AS4c14, AS5c20). They set the maximum of the unfiltered trace in 6 of the 14 VENs and 4 of the 21 PCs under the baseline-subtracted reading a2 b1 c1, 9 of the 10 in session 221206AS, so a peak taken without a filter measures them, not the Na+ current.

In the paper's code repository, the two blocks of sumData_StimWM.xlsx that hold the eEPSP amplitudes of Fig. 4j ("copied data" and "re-orgnized data") agree in 69 of 78 rows and differ in 9; the re-organized block reproduces the paper's P = 0.0034 (0.0033). The script extFig9ad_plotVENsubtypeAP_Cmp.m loads VENsubtype_APs.mat from a folder VENsubtypeCmp_extFig9ab that is not in the repository, which holds it under VENsubtypeCmp_extFig8ab.

disagreements.reason: Only the four a1 readings give a ratio within 0.6875 +/- 0.069 under some summary (0.68 to 0.75). All a2 readings fall outside (0.79 to 0.99), and so does the code table (0.58 mean, 0.51 median). The a1 ratios carry the holding-current offset and the parent claim is blocked, so this "partial" is weak.

It is left blocked although part of it can be tested. Column J of the same sheet types 24 of the 26 pairs as VENL or VENS (12 each at every stimulation level), which matches the Extended Data Fig. 9f design, so the VEN-L vs VEN-S eEPSP ANOVA (paper p = 0.9852) can be run.

entries.name: 001750-liu-2026
entries.title: Somatic Na+ currents of VENs and PCs in macaque insular cortex (Liu et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Liu, Huang, Shen, Shao, Jing et al. (2026) that rest on dandiset 001750, which holds 35 outside-out patch recordings of somatic Na+ currents from one macaque. It links the files to the paper's per-cell table, compares the maximal Na+ current of VENs and L5 PCs under each reading of the method, and checks the VEN to PC ratio and the patch size. It also tests the metabolomics findings on MetaboLights MTBLS13927, and the eEPSP amplitude ANOVA, the VEN subtype comparisons and the phase peak index comparison on the paper's own tables.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Liu et al. (2026) from dandiset 001750

entries.name: 001752-liu-2026
entries.title: Synaptic currents of von Economo neurons and pyramidal cells in macaque insular cortex (Liu et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the Fig. 5a-c findings of Liu, Huang, Shen, Shao, Jing et al. (2026) on dandiset 001752, which holds 84 voltage-clamp recordings of spontaneous and miniature EPSCs and IPSCs from VENs and pyramidal cells of the macaque anterior insular cortex. Events are detected in each recording and their frequency and amplitude compared between cell types, with the cell types taken from the table of deposited files in the paper's code. A second notebook tests claims whose data are elsewhere, on the code's per-cell tables, the sodium-current dandiset 001750, the Patch-seq electrophysiology dandiset 001746, the metadata of the multi-patch dandiset 001751 and the metabolomics deposit MetaboLights MTBLS13927.
